common_name: Red Peacock Chinese Evergreen (Deep Red Aglaonema)

planting.note: Grow year-round as an indoor foliage plant in bright, indirect light; move to a shaded porch or patio in summer once nights stay reliably above 55F.

directions: Red Peacock belongs to the group of Thai-bred red-leaf Chinese evergreens introduced alongside better-known cultivars like Red Gold and Siam Aurora, all selected from Aglaonema commutatum and rotundum parentage for intense pigment. Its lance-shaped leaves emerge a saturated rosy red along the veins and margins, deepening further under bright indirect light, while the central blade stays a darker olive green that frames the color. The plant forms a dense, upright clump that rarely tops 20 inches, making it a manageable size for tabletops, desks, or grouped dish arrangements. Keep it out of direct sun, which can bleach the red pigment, let the top inch of soil dry between waterings, and protect it from temperatures below 55F.

planting.note: Grow year-round as a compact indoor foliage plant in low to bright indirect light; move to a shaded spot outdoors only after nights stay reliably above 55F.

directions: Cutlass takes its name from its distinctively narrow, elongated, blade-like leaves, a departure from the broader oval foliage typical of most Chinese evergreen cultivars. Each leaf is brushed with silvery-grey mottling over a deep green base, and the slender form gives the whole plant a more upright, grassy silhouette than rounder-leaved relatives such as Silver Queen. It grows as a dense, clumping houseplant well suited to narrow spaces like hallway shelves or between pieces of furniture where broader foliage plants would crowd. Grow in low to bright indirect light, allow the top of the potting mix to dry slightly between waterings, and keep it away from cold drafts and temperatures below 55F.

common_name: Jubilee Compact Chinese Evergreen (Dwarf Pink-Variegated Aglaonema)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a small-footprint indoor foliage plant in medium to bright indirect light; it stays compact enough for dish gardens and small containers without needing to move outdoors.

directions: Jubilee Compact is a dwarf form of the larger Jubilee aglaonema, grown for carrying the parent's bold pink-and-green mottled leaf pattern on a much smaller, denser plant. Its broad, pointed leaves show irregular splashes of rose pink and cream over dark green, with new growth often emerging more vividly pink before settling into its mature pattern. The tight, clumping habit and reduced mature size make it a popular choice for dish gardens, terrariums, and small container groupings where a full-size Jubilee would quickly outgrow its space. Provide bright indirect light to keep the pink coloring strong, let the top inch of potting mix dry between waterings, and protect the plant from temperatures below 55F.

common_name: Golden Madonna Chinese Evergreen (Cream-Gold Variegated Aglaonema)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a medium-size indoor foliage plant in low to bright indirect light; move to a shaded patio in summer once nights stay reliably above 55F.

directions: Golden Madonna is one of the older named aglaonema hybrids that, alongside cultivars like Silver Queen, helped popularize variegated Chinese evergreens as houseplants starting in the 1980s. Its broad, pointed leaves carry an irregular pattern of creamy yellow-gold blotching over medium green, giving the plant a warmer, sunnier look than the cooler silver-grey tones of Silver Queen or Silver Bay. It forms a sturdy, upright clump of medium height and has proven durable under the low to moderate light common in offices and interior plantscapes. Grow in low to bright indirect light, water when the top inch of soil has dried, and keep it above 55F to avoid cold-induced leaf spotting.
